inherits: docs/research/real_telemetry_protocol_v1.json (rt1); rt1 is retained unchanged, including its failed primary rule
motivation: rt1 found that a normal-only world-model residual detector (D1) caught 44 of 58 recorded HAI 22.04 attacks at about one false alarm episode per day, far above persistence and bound/gradient baselines, while the incident-informed classifier (D2) failed its registered rule. A labelled post-hoc analysis (docs/research/real_telemetry_posthoc_rt1.json) showed that at a matched test false-alarm rate D2 ranked attacks best (47/58 versus 44/58), so its failure came from threshold transfer: its calibrated threshold sat at the 99.999th percentile of normal test scores. rt2 tests both findings prospectively on two HAI releases whose attacks have never been opened.

hai-21.03.final: test1-5.csv.gz with the per-second attack label

data.manifest: docs/research/real_telemetry_data_manifest_v1.json (same repository and pinned commit as HAI 22.04; files verified against Git LFS oids or Git blob hashes)
data.actions: rt1's HAI_ACTIONS plus the release-specific setpoint, demand and command tags P2_ASD, P2_MSD, P2_CO_rpm, P3_LH, P3_LL, P1_PP04D and the 23.05 DCS outputs named x10*_SETPOINT_OUT, x10*_ASSIGN_OUT and x10*_SUM_OUT; all other varying tags are sensors; constant training tags are dropped.
data.partitions: Training files in chronological order are cut at 50% and 80% of total normal time: world-model fit, detector training, calibration and selection.
data.final_access_rule: Test files and labels are read only through real_telemetry_rt2.test_segments, which appends to target/real-telemetry/final_access.jsonl. Neither release has an entry before the rt2 selection freeze. The final evaluation runs once.

method.unchanged_from_rt1: real_telemetry_core, real_telemetry_injections and the Scorer, classifier, smoothing grid, episode-budget calibration and seeds of real_telemetry_detect at commit 53de7a9.
method.world_model: Fixed to rt1's selected HAI class: ridge plus LightGBM residual corrections, action-conditioned, horizons 1 and 5, history 3. No re-selection.
detectors: D2 incident-informed classifier (rt1 design and calibration)
D2c: D2 scores with the threshold set so that D2's clean-calibration alarm fraction equals D1's calibrated clean alarm fraction (registered calibration fix)
method.calibration: 2 false alarm episodes per day of clean calibration data, merge gap 60 s; smoothing window per detector from {1, 10, 60} by injected development-family validation recall; D2c uses D2's window.

gates.primary_hypothesis: Replication of rt1's world-model finding. For each release, D1 versus D0 and D1 versus DR: relative miss reduction at least 20% and the lower bound of the 98.75% paired event-bootstrap interval (10,000 resamples; Bonferroni across 2 releases x 2 baselines) above zero; and D1's final false-alarm rate at most 4 episodes per day.
gates.secondary: For each release, D2c versus D1 and D2 versus D1 relative miss reduction with 95% paired event-bootstrap intervals; D2c is called an improvement over D1 only if its interval lower bound is above zero and its final false-alarm rate is at most 4 episodes per day. D3 versus D1 and D2c versus D3 are reported.
gates.reporting: All detectors, both releases and all failures are reported. No claim of runtime authority, deployment safety or real-incident prevention follows.

limitations_registered_in_advance: All three HAI releases come from one testbed and one group of attack designers; rt2 is a within-testbed replication, not an independent-site replication.
The D2c rule was chosen after seeing rt1's test results; rt2's unopened releases are its only test.
The author viewed the HAI technical manual's attack table before rt1; targeting stays random.
